list: Listen to your own footsteps for ten steps.
Find the thing with the longest shadow.
Go five minutes without looking at your phone.
Of the signs you see today, pick the lettering you like best.
Count the steps on a staircase.
Close your eyes and pick out three different sounds.
Find three round things.
Give today’s sky a name.
Remember the quietest moment of today.
Pick your favorite green of the day.
Give a name to a corner you always pass.
Find the oldest-looking thing around you.
Remember the brightest moment of today.
Count the white stripes on a crosswalk.
Put your phone at the bottom of your bag for thirty minutes.
Look at someone’s shoes and imagine where they’re headed.
If it rains, listen to the rain on your umbrella.
Look at your room as if you were visiting for the first time.
Leave your phone face down for an hour.
Record your own voice and listen to it.
Find five blue things.
Find the farthest thing you can see.
Tell apart two kinds of birdsong.
Step outside and put the first smell you notice into words.
Put a hand on your chest and count ten heartbeats.
Imagine the name of the person walking ahead of you.
Wonder where today’s clouds will be tomorrow.
Guess the time without checking your phone.
Ride one stop without taking out your phone.
For ten minutes before bed, leave your phone in another room.
If the moon is out, remember its shape.
Remember the coldest wind you feel today.
Find the tallest building you can see.
Spot the number 7 three times.
Listen for the smallest sound around you.
Remember the best bite you eat today.
Brush your teeth with your other hand.
See your everyday station or stop through a tourist’s eyes.
Make up your own lyrics to a tune you overhear.
Give a name to an animal you see.
Imagine where you are right now from above, like a bird.
Don’t look at your phone during a meal.
Next time you’re waiting, keep your phone put away.
At dusk, catch the moment the streetlights come on.
Tell someone what color the sky is today.
Pick one moment from today that you might remember ten years from now.
Say “thank you” to someone you don’t usually thank.
